rules.statement: Don't ask for rewording, restructuring or other edits to a template-owned or protected file whose text is copied word for word from project-template; any fix belongs in the template.
rules.why: Later template updates compare against the project's copy, so a local rewording makes the copy differ from the template's text and gets in the way of those updates.
rules.check: Before reporting wording in a file such as a workflow header or a criteria page, check whether project-template owns it, for example whether it matches a template release word for word or is listed as template-owned. If it does, don't report it against this repository.

rules.statement: Don't ask a changelog entry to add a 'project-template' prefix to the link text of a template ADR when the existing entries link template records without one and the link path points into the template's decisions folder.
rules.why: Template records are numbered below 1000 and the project's from 1000, so the number names one record and the link path shows it is a template record. The new entry follows the style of the existing entries.
rules.check: Compare the new entry's link text with how the existing CHANGELOG.md entries cite template ADRs, and check that the link target is under docs/decisions/project-template/. If they match, don't report it.

rules.statement: Don't report a pull request description as understating its scope because it doesn't list each edit to template-owned files, when the description already says those files pick up a template update.
rules.why: Edits to template-owned files come from the template update itself, and the description covers them where it names that update.
rules.check: Before reporting that the description leaves out a change, check whether the changed file is template-owned and whether the description mentions the template version update that brings in the change.
